sources.title: Bone spoons for prehistoric babies — Stefanović et al., PLOS ONE (2019)
Spoon, 12.187.30 — The Metropolitan Museum of Art

notes: 勺子没有可确认的单一发明者或发源地，且存在早于本条所选遗址的零星记录。时间轴采用格拉德—斯塔尔切沃遗址前5800—前5450年断代范围的起点，不代表精确发明年份。2019年研究将部分骨勺磨痕与实验获得的乳牙痕迹比较，支持婴幼儿喂食用途。地图点为出土地一带的示意。埃及象牙勺的馆藏断代为前3100—前2649年。
notes_en: Spoons have no established single inventor or birthplace, and isolated earlier finds exist. The timeline uses the start of the Grad-Starčevo site’s 5800–5450 BCE date range, not an exact invention date. A 2019 study compared wear with experimental milk-tooth marks, supporting infant feeding. Pins approximate findspots. The Egyptian ivory spoon dates to ca. 3100–2649 BCE.
summary_zh: 勺子在史前已经出现，起源难以归于一地。塞尔维亚前5800—前5450年的骨勺上，发现了与婴幼儿乳牙吻合的痕迹；埃及也留下了约前3100—前2649年的象牙勺实物。
summary_en: Prehistoric spoons have no single known birthplace. Serbian bone spoons from 5800–5450 BCE bear marks matching milk teeth; an Egyptian ivory spoon dates to ca. 3100–2649 BCE.
